title: Semaglutide-associated risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
authors: Chrzanowski J, Walicka M, Burzyński J, Zaraś M, Michalak A, Fendler W
population: Five eligible observational studies of semaglutide against other glucose-lowering therapy in type 2 diabetes, with seven more in sensitivity analyses; search January 2023 to November 2025
funder: Authors were supported by the Foundation for Polish Science, the Medical University of Lodz, the National Science Centre of Poland, the Kościuszko Foundation, Diabetes Poland and other public programmes; the funding was not associated with article preparation and the funders had no role in design, collection, analysis, the decision to publish or preparation of the manuscript.
authorConflicts: Two authors received lecture honoraria from Novo Nordisk and Boehringer Ingelheim, one also a consulting fee from Novo Nordisk; one received lecture honoraria from AstraZeneca, Eli Lilly, Sanofi and Teva.
result: Semaglutide was associated with a higher hazard of NAION against non-semaglutide regimens (hazard ratio 2.17, 95% CI 1.73 to 2.74), regimens excluding other GLP-1 receptor agonists (2.13, 1.60 to 2.83) and SGLT2 inhibitors (1.96, 1.28 to 2.99). Absolute risk increase 0.014% (0.005% to 0.023%), about one additional case per 7000 semaglutide-treated patients per year. Certainty of evidence low, with possible outcome misclassification and confounding.
